title: Homily III — A new exodus song, and why she had to die

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily III on the Dormition, col. 757 (PDF leaf 420)

source_text:
Φευγέτωσαν δαίμονες, ὀλολυζέτωσαν τρισάθλιοι Νεστώριοι, ὡς πρόπαλαι οἱ Αἰγύπτιοι, καὶ ὁ τούτων ἔξαρχος ὁ νέος Φαραώ, ὁ πικρὸς ἀλάστωρ καὶ τύραννος. Τῷ βυθῷ γὰρ τῆς βλασφημίας κατεχώσθησαν. Ἡμεῖς δὲ οἱ σωθέντες ἀβρόχοις ποσίν, καὶ τὴν ἁλμυρὰν τῆς ἀσεβείας ὑπερβάντες θάλασσαν, ᾄσωμεν τῇ Μητρὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ ᾠδὴν τὴν ἐξόδιον.

Αἱρέτω Μαριὰμ ἡ Ἐκκλησία ταῖς χερσὶ τὸ τύμπανον, καὶ ἐξαρχέτω ᾠδὴν τὴν ἑόρτιον. Ἐξίτωσαν τοῦ πνευματικοῦ Ἰσραὴλ αἱ νεάνιδες μετὰ τυμπάνων καὶ χορῶν ἀλαλάζουσαι. Βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς καὶ κριταὶ σὺν ἄρχουσι, νεανίσκοι καὶ παρθένοι, πρεσβῦται μετὰ νεωτέρων, τὴν Θεοτόκον ὑμνείτωσαν, σύλλογοι, καὶ λόγοι παντοδαποί, καὶ ἐθνῶν καὶ λαῶν γλῶσσαι διάφοροι, ᾆσμα καινὸν μελουργείτωσαν. Περιηχείτω ἀὴρ πνευματικοῖς δόναξί τε καὶ σάλπιγξι, καὶ τοῖς ἐκ πυρὸς ἀμαρύγμασιν ἡμέραν καινουργείτω σωτήριον. Εὐφράνθητε, οὐρανοί, καὶ αἱ νεφέλαι ῥανάτωσαν ἀγαλλίασιν. Σκιρτήσατε, κριοὶ τῆς ἐκλεκτῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ ποίμνης, οἱ θεῖοι ἀπόστολοι, ὡς ὄρη ὑψηλὰ καὶ μετέωρα ταῖς ὑψηλοτάταις θεωρίαις ὑψούμενοι, καὶ ἄρνες Θεοῦ, λαὸς ἅγιος, τῆς Ἐκκλησίας τὰ θρέμματα, ὥσπερ βουνοὶ πρὸς τὰ ὑψηλὰ ὄρη τῇ προαιρέσει ἀνατεινόμενοι.

Βαβαί! βαβαί! τέθνηκεν ἡ πηγὴ τῆς ζωῆς, ἡ τοῦ Κυρίου μου Μήτηρ; Ἔδει γὰρ τὸ ἐκ γῆς συντεθὲν παλινοστῆσαι πρὸς γῆν, καὶ οὕτω μεταναστῆναι πρὸς οὐρανόν, ἐκ τῆς γῆς λαβὼν τὴν δεδωρημένην τῇ γῇ τῇ καταθέσει τοῦ σώματος παναχήρατον ζωήν. Ἔδει γὰρ καθάπερ χρυσὸν ἀποβαλοῦσαν τὸ γεῶδες καὶ ἀλαμπὲς τῆς θνητότητος πάχος, ὡς ἐν χωνεύσει τῷ θανάτῳ τὴν σάρκα ἄφθαρτον καὶ καθαράν, τῷ φέγγει τῆς ἀφθαρσίας ἐκλάμπουσαν ἐξαναστῆναι τοῦ μνήματος.
pass_a_gloss: [0] Let flee demons, let wail thrice-wretched Nestorians, as long ago the Egyptians, and the leader (ἔξαρχος) of these, the new Pharaoh (Φαραώ), the bitter (πικρός) avenger/destroyer (ἀλάστωρ) and tyrant (τύραννος). For in the depth (βυθός) of blasphemy they were buried/heaped over. But we, the ones saved (σωθέντες) with unwetted (ἀβρόχοις) feet, and having crossed over the salt (ἁλμυρά) sea of impiety (ἀσέβεια), let us sing (ᾄσωμεν) to the Mother of God the exodus/funeral song. [1] Let take up (αἱρέτω) Miriam (Μαριάμ) the Church (Ἐκκλησία) in the hands the timbrel (τύμπανον), and let her lead off (ἐξαρχέτω) the festal (ἑόρτιος) song. Let go out (ἐξίτωσαν) the young women (νεάνιδες) of the spiritual Israel with timbrels and dances (χοροί) shouting aloud. Kings of the earth and judges (κριταί) with rulers (ἄρχοντες), young men and virgins (παρθένοι), elders with younger, let them hymn the Theotokos (Θεοτόκος); assemblies (σύλλογοι) and words (λόγοι) of every kind, and differing tongues of nations and peoples, let them compose a new song. Let the air resound around with spiritual reeds (δόνακες) and trumpets, and with the flashings from fire let it make new a saving (σωτήριον) day. Be glad, heavens, and let the clouds sprinkle exultation. Leap, rams (κριοί) of the chosen (ἐκλεκτή) flock (ποίμνη) of God, the divine apostles, as mountains high and lofty with the highest contemplations (θεωρίαι) being raised, and lambs (ἄρνες) of God, holy people (λαός), the nurslings (θρέμματα) of the Church, like hills (βουνοί) toward the high mountains by choice/will stretching up. [2] Babai, babai! Has died (τέθνηκεν) the spring (πηγή) of life, the Mother of my Lord? For it was necessary (ἔδει) that the thing composed (συντεθέν) from earth return home to earth, and so move over to heaven, from the earth taking the all-pure life granted [to the earth / in the earth] by the deposition of the body. For it was necessary that, like gold (χρυσός), having cast off the earthy (γεῶδες) and unshining (ἀλαμπές) thickness (πάχος) of mortality (θνητότης), as in smelting (χώνευσις) by death, the flesh (σάρξ) incorrupt (ἄφθαρτος) and pure (καθαρά), shining with the light (φέγγος) of incorruption (ἀφθαρσία), she rise up out of the tomb (μνῆμα).
pass_b_english: Let the demons flee; let the thrice-wretched Nestorians and their leader, the new Pharaoh, the bitter destroyer and tyrant, wail as the Egyptians did long ago. For they have been buried in the depths of their blasphemy (Exodus 15:4–5). But let us who were saved with dry feet (Exodus 14:29) and have crossed the salt sea of ungodliness sing to the Mother of God the song of her exodus.

Let Miriam, the Church, take the timbrel in her hands and lead off the festal song (Exodus 15:20–21). Let the young women of the spiritual Israel go out with timbrels and dances, shouting for joy. Kings of the earth and judges with rulers, young men and virgins, old men with the younger (Psalm 148:11–12): let them sing hymns to the Mother of God. Let assemblies, and words of every kind, and the varied tongues of nations and peoples compose a new song. Let the air resound all around with spiritual reeds and trumpets, and let it fashion a new day of salvation with flashes of fire. Rejoice, you heavens, and let the clouds rain down gladness (Isaiah 45:8). Leap, you rams of God's chosen flock, you divine apostles, raised up like high and lofty mountains by the loftiest contemplations; and you lambs of God, holy people, nurslings of the Church, like hills reaching up by your own choice toward the high mountains (Psalm 114:4).

Ah! Ah! Has the fountain of life died, the Mother of my Lord (Luke 1:43)? Yes, for what was put together from earth had to return to earth (Genesis 3:19), and so pass over to heaven, receiving from the earth, through the laying of her body in it, the gift of a life wholly pure. For like gold she had to cast off the earthy and lustreless thickness of mortality, and, with death as the furnace, to rise from the tomb with her flesh incorrupt and pure, shining with the light of incorruption.

choices.note: No Scripture margin numbers on this leaf; all citations are clear unmarked allusions.
Exodus 14-15: the Egyptians and Pharaoh drowned, Israel crossing on dry ground (14:29), the song at the sea, Miriam's timbrel (15:20-21).
Psalm 148:11-12 follows the LXX wording closely (same number in LXX and English).
Isaiah 45:8 LXX ('let the clouds sprinkle righteousness'): John substitutes 'gladness' (ἀγαλλίασιν); the English keeps his word.
Psalm 114:4 (and 114:6) = LXX/Vulgate Psalm 113:4 (mountains leaping like rams, hills like lambs).
Luke 1:43 cited for 'the Mother of my Lord' (Elizabeth's words, exact Greek order reversed).
Left uncited: 'a new song' (Psalm 96:1, 98:1, Isaiah 42:10 and others; no single target).
Genesis 3:19 cited inline for 'what was put together from earth had to return to earth' (the verse quoted in 3.2).
ἔδει rendered 'had to' (necessity), not 'it was right'.
Readings: ᾠδὴν τὴν ἐξόδιον means both 'song of departure' and 'funeral song' and plays on the exodus at the sea; rendered 'the song of her exodus'.
'Αἱρέτω Μαριὰμ ἡ Ἐκκλησία' is printed as one phrase; rendered 'Let Miriam, the Church, take', keeping the Church as the new Miriam.
ἀλάστωρ ('avenging spirit, destroyer';
Latin 'orbis depopulator') rendered 'destroyer'.
The 'new Pharaoh' is Nestorius: Migne's note (68) gives the Seguier reading 'and the hostile Nestorius the tyrant, buried in the depth of his foul blasphemy'; the English follows the print.
'their blasphemy' supplies the possessive implied by the article (τῆς βλασφημίας).
Βαβαί is an exclamation of wonder or grief; rendered 'Ah! Ah!'.
'Yes, for' renders the answering γάρ after the question.
λαβών (masculine) is printed where the neuter λαβόν would agree with τὸ συντεθέν (Migne note 69); sense unchanged.
'τὴν δεδωρημένην τῇ γῇ τῇ καταθέσει τοῦ σώματος ...

ζωήν' is ambiguous: either 'the life granted through the laying of the body in the earth' (followed here, with the Latin 'post corporis in terra depositionem') or 'the life given to the earth by the laying of her body'; the English 'receiving from the earth, through the laying of her body in it, the gift of a life wholly pure' leans to the first.
τὴν σάρκα ...
ἐκλάμπουσαν taken as accusative of respect ('with her flesh incorrupt').
